title: T0002 Surgery and LITT seizure-outcome evidence (resection vs laser ablation, drug-resistant focal epilepsy)
body:
## Scope and search
Searched Europe PMC REST (title/author/abstract queries for TLE surgery RCTs, ERSET, long-term surgery outcome meta-analyses and cohorts, LITT multicenter/prospective studies, LITT meta-analyses; no date limit) plus web search for the SLATE trial. 15 sources opened and screened in full-abstract form (stop rule 25; other titles were triaged from search lists only). 14 sources kept, each committed as one EvidenceClaim (A0017-A0030). All passages were checked verbatim against the Europe PMC abstractText. The SLATE passage was checked against the AES abstract page. **Abstracts only were read; no full texts.** Endpoint definitions and follow-up that the abstracts leave out are marked not_reported or to_verify.

## 1. Open resection (mainly temporal)
**RCTs: 3 study families, n=234 randomised in total.**
- Wiebe 2001 (A0017): adult TLE, n=80. 58% vs 8% free of seizures impairing awareness at 1 year.
- ERSET 2012 (A0018): early mesial TLE, age >=12, n=38, stopped early. 11/15 vs 0/23 seizure free in year 2 (73% vs 0%).
- Dwivedi 2017 (A0019): **paediatric-only**, n=116, mixed procedures. 77% vs 7% seizure free at 12 months, with 33% serious adverse events. Analyse separately per the protocol.

All three RCTs compare surgery with medical therapy, not with LITT. The endpoints are 'free of disabling seizures / seizures impairing awareness', which approximates Engel I (favourable under mapping v1).

**Long-term observational evidence:**
- Tellez-Zenteno 2005 MA (A0020): 83 studies, no RCTs, follow-up >=5 years. Median seizure-free proportion 66% for temporal, 46% for occipital/parietal and 27% for frontal resections.
- de Tisi 2011 (A0021): n=615 adults, median follow-up 8 years. Kaplan-Meier continuous seizure freedom (apart from SPS) 52% at 5 years and 47% at 10 years. Extratemporal resections had more recurrence than ATL (HR 2.0).
- The two figures disagree mainly because they define seizure freedom differently (survival/time-to-first-seizure vs cross-sectional).
- Ekman 2024 MA (A0027): temporal lobe resection in MTLE had 72.5% (65.6-78.5) seizure freedom at >24 months.

**Range for temporal resection: about 47-77% seizure free at >=1 year, depending on definition and horizon. Extratemporal resection is consistently lower.**

## 2. Laser interstitial thermal therapy (mostly mesial TLE)
**No RCT located. A prospective randomised protocol (MINE, China, 2026) was seen in search results but not opened or committed.**
- SLATE (A0024): prospective single-arm study, 21 US sites, 167 enrolled, 114 followed 12 months. Engel I 55.9% at 12 months (lower 95% confidence limit 45.9%). **Conference abstract only; no peer-reviewed results paper found.**
- Wu 2019 (A0022): 11-centre retrospective cohort, n=234. 58.0% Engel I at 1 and 2 years. Ablation location (amygdala, anterior/medial) predicted outcome.
- Gross 2018 Emory (A0023): n=58. 53.4% Engel I at 1 year (MTS 60.5% vs non-MTS 33.3%).
- Kerezoudis 2020 MA (A0025): 13 studies, n=551, TLE. 58% pooled seizure freedom overall and 66% in MTS. Follow-up not reported in the abstract.
- Chen 2023 IPD-MA (A0026): 46 studies, n=450, mixed DRE. 57.8% seizure free at last follow-up (median 19 months). CCM and MTS predicted success; nonlesional MRI predicted recurrence.

**Range for LITT: about 53-58% Engel I / seizure free at 1-2 years in MTLE (5 study families; the meta-analyses overlap, so count them as 1 pooled family).**

## 3. Head-to-head LITT vs open surgery (non-randomised)
- Ekman 2024 (A0027), MTLE, >24 months: resection 72.5% vs LITT 57.1% (P<0.01).
- Pichardo-Rojas 2026 (A0028): 15 comparative cohorts, n=3873. LITT 52.5% vs open 67.1% (RR 0.78, 0.70-0.88). **No significant difference** in propensity-matched studies (RR 0.85) or in TLE studies (RR 0.88).
- Maroufi 2026 (A0029): nontumoral epilepsy, 11 studies, 389 LITT vs 557 open. 53.7% vs 68.1% (RR 0.81, p=0.07, not significant).

Across all three, LITT has fewer complications and shorter stays. **The three meta-analyses disagree on whether the seizure-freedom gap persists after matching.** This is flagged in the contradictions fields.

## 4. Guideline
AES/CNS 2026 GRADE guideline (A0030):
- **Strong** recommendation, moderate certainty: ATL for MTLE at low cognitive risk.
- **Conditional**, very low to low certainty: SAH and LITT in MTLE, and neocortical resection.
- Neurostimulation was not addressed.

## Bottom line for the study question (surgery/ablation arm)
- Resection for temporal-lobe DRE is the only intervention here with RCT support against medical therapy: 3 RCTs, large effects, 58-77% seizure free at 1-2 years.
- Long-term durability is about 47-66% at 5-10 years.
- LITT gives about 55-58% Engel I at 1-2 years from 1 prospective single-arm study plus retrospective cohorts. It looks numerically lower than open resection in unmatched comparisons; matched comparisons are inconclusive.
- Under protocol mapping v1, most outcomes reported here map to 'favourable' (Engel I / seizure free). Wiebe's endpoint is an approximation.
- **The >=5 comparable-study condition for pooling is met only for LITT single-arm proportions, and those come from overlapping meta-analyses. Recommend ranges rather than a new pooled estimate.**

## Study-family and overlap notes
- The LITT meta-analyses (A0025-A0029) share the family fam-litt-pooled-meta-analyses and must not be counted as independent. They very likely include Gross 2018 and possibly Wu 2019 cohorts (to_verify).
- SLATE shares sites with Wu 2019 (possible patient overlap).
- Tellez-Zenteno 2005 may include earlier reports of the NHNN cohort behind de Tisi 2011.
- The guideline is a synthesis of the same primary studies.

## Indeterminate / not verified
- Full texts were not read.
- Follow-up length and seizure-freedom definition are not reported in the Kerezoudis, Pichardo-Rojas and Maroufi abstracts.
- The SLATE denominator and funding are unconfirmed, and no SLATE peer-reviewed publication was located.
- Engel vs ILAE classes are not separable from the abstracts for most meta-analyses.
